## Description

`/dso:fix-bug` (and analogous fix-style remediation flows) implements NEW behavior — adding application features that modify intent — without user confirmation, framing the new feature as a bug fix or DD-coverage remediation.

## Evidence (session 2026-05-18)

After story 5621's completion-verifier reported a 'DD4 gap: DISPATCH_NEXT branch missing PR comment with text Cycle K complete; N findings remain; awaiting next push for cycle K+1', the orchestrator AUTO-FILED remediation task ddb5-be9d-45b1-4246 and dispatched a fix-style agent that ADDED a new helper to runner.py and posted a new PR comment marker that did not previously exist. No user confirmation was sought.

Tracking history:
- Original epic: b575-ac1c-f720-4839
- Original ticket: e486-2d01-9443-40ac (closed; this is the recreation without parent)
- Triggering task: ddb5-be9d-45b1-4246 (closed; code being reverted)

## Why this is P0

- User has repeatedly stated that fix-bug and fix-style flows must NOT add new features
- Pattern silently expands epic scope, making it impossible to predict what will change
- CLAUDE.md additions for this rule are rejected by user as ineffective (agents ignore CLAUDE.md)
- This bug requires DEDICATED focused work post-remediation with enforcement mechanisms that don't depend on agent compliance (pre-commit hooks, tool-use gates, completion-verifier interpretation discipline)

## Expected behavior

When a fix-style remediation would ADD new application behavior (new comment posting, new API calls, new user-visible artifacts, new gates), the skill must STOP and ask the user to confirm scope before proceeding. Completion-verifier DD interpretations are HINTS, not authorization to add new behavior.

## Resolution path

Address with dedicated focus AFTER the remediation epic stabilizes the PR/review workflow. Do not attempt CLAUDE.md-based mitigations. Real enforcement options to investigate: pre-commit hooks, tool-use gates, completion-verifier scope-classification rubric.
data.title: /dso:fix-bug implements features (new behavior) under guise of 'fixing'
